title: An exact and fast solution of the inverse Regularized Optimal Transport problem
authors: Dario Mazzilli, Riccardo Piombo, Lorenzo Buffa, Aurelio Patelli
abstract: Optimal transport describes the most efficient way to move mass between two distributions, given a cost matrix for moving mass between each pair of locations. Entropic optimal transport, solved via the Sinkhorn algorithm, is a widely used regularized version of this problem. Its inverse problem asks the opposite question: given an observed transport plan, what cost matrix produced it? This is difficult because the cost is identifiable only up to an additive gauge freedom. Here we show that this freedom can be fixed exactly by a single double-centering operation applied to the observed plan, yielding the true cost matrix in closed form, with no iterative optimization required. When a modest number of true cost entries are known, the same approach lets us jointly estimate the temperature parameter controlling the entropic regularization, together with a diagnostic for the reliability of this estimate. We further show that the method is not specific to the entropic optimal transport, but extends to a broader class of transport models defined by an invertible relation between cost and plan.
summary: This work solves the difficult inverse problem in Optimal Transport by proposing an exact, non-iterative method based on a double-centering operation. This technique uniquely reconstructs the true cost matrix from an observed transport plan, bypassing the need to solve the forward OT problem iteratively. It provides a powerful, general tool for inferring underlying physical costs from empirical transport data.
main_problem: The paper addresses the inverse problem of Optimal Transport (OT): recovering the underlying cost matrix given an observed optimal transport plan. This is challenging due to inherent gauge freedom in the cost structure.
main_result: The authors provide an exact, closed-form solution using a single double-centering operation to uniquely fix the gauge freedom and recover the cost matrix without iterative optimization. This method is general and extends beyond entropic regularization.
method: The core method involves applying a double-centering operation to the observed plan (or its transform) to remove additive row and column gauge contributions, yielding a canonical cost matrix representation.
model_or_system: The framework is based on Optimal Transport (OT) and its regularized version, Entropic Optimal Transport (EOT). The problem is framed as recovering the cost matrix $C$ from the transport plan $W$ that minimizes the regularized energy.
key_observables: The recovered cost matrix ($ ar{C}'$), the temperature parameter ($\epsilon$), and diagnostics like the Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) are key observables.
important_parameters: The regularization temperature $\epsilon$, the size of the marginals ($N, M$), and the noise level ($\sigma$) are important parameters.
main_assumptions: The method assumes the existence of an invertible relation between the cost and the plan, and it is robust to multiplicative noise in the observed plan $W$.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the double-centering operation on distance matrices and compare reconstruction errors based on the number of independent cycles in the observed data graph.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the inverse OT problem and the gauge freedom. It then introduces the double-centering technique as the exact solution. Subsequent sections detail its application to estimate parameters like $\epsilon$ and analyze reconstruction accuracy under partial information and noise.
why_interesting: While the topic is mathematical statistics/optimization, the underlying structure of OT is deeply connected to quantum information geometry and quantum state estimation, making the rigorous mathematical tools relevant to quantum physics.
